hints: Notice the pipe is open at one end and closed at the other, so there must be a displacement node at the closed end and an antinode at the open end.
Lowest frequency means longest wavelength, which for this pipe is the quarter-wavelength mode where the $10 \text{ m}$ length equals $\lambda/4$.
Combine $\lambda = 4L$ with the wave equation $v = f\lambda$ using $v = 320 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $L = 10 \text{ m}$.
walkthrough: Identify the stationary wave condition: closed end is a displacement node and open end is a displacement antinode.
For the lowest frequency, the fundamental, only one quarter of a wavelength fits in the pipe, so $L = \lambda/4$.
Use $v = f\lambda$ rearranged to $f = v/\lambda$ with $v = 320 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Substitute: $f = 320/40 = 8 \text{ Hz}$ with unit $\text{Hz}$ as required for frequency. This is option B.

options.A: Gives half the correct frequency, corresponding to $\lambda = 80 \text{ m}$, which is twice the longest wavelength that fits a $10 \text{ m}$ closed-open pipe.
options.B: The fundamental has $L = \lambda/4$, so $\lambda = 40 \text{ m}$ and $f = v/\lambda = 320/40 = 8 \text{ Hz}$.
options.C: Uses $L = \lambda/2$ which applies to a pipe open at both ends, giving $\lambda = 20 \text{ m}$ and $16 \text{ Hz}$.
options.D: Uses $L = \lambda$, giving $\lambda = 10 \text{ m}$ and $32 \text{ Hz}$, which does not satisfy the node-antinode end conditions.
